title: Reporting Promptness Terms for Late Delivery Claims
content:
Under Delivery Claims, the delivery-charge refund on a Late Delivery Claim reflects how soon after delivery the customer reported the late parcel.

**Term.** The reporting share depends on how soon the claim was opened: a claim opened 15 or more calendar days after the delivered date pays 80% of the basis, one opened 8 to 14 calendar days after it pays 90%, and one opened within 7 calendar days pays the whole basis.

The days are the calendar days from the order's delivered date to the date the claim was opened, as each is recorded.

| Calendar days from delivered date to opening | Share of the basis paid |
|---|---|
| 0 to 7 | 100% — the whole basis |
| 8 to 14 | 90% |
| 15 or more | 80% |

## Edges of each band (hypothetical delivered date of 1 September)

| Claim opened on | Days after delivery | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 1 September | 0 | 100% |
| 8 September | 7 | 100% |
| 9 September | 8 | 90% |
| 15 September | 14 | 90% |
| 16 September | 15 | 80% |
| 30 September | 29 | 80% |

On a hypothetical basis of 30.00 USD, a claim opened 10 days after delivery is paid 90% of the basis, 27.00 USD, on this term.
